dlg.wayfinder.first.0.hides: she sells the names of those who come back, to feed her brother in his cage
dlg.wayfinder.first.0.note: Brisk Edinburgh. The joke about the other sort is dry, a cartographer's sales line, no relish. 'barrows' a touch faster, no weight: it's her brother's. The last two sentences drier and darker.
dlg.wayfinder.first.0.beats: You've the look of someone who comes back. [beat] Good. The other sort only ever buy the one map. [breath] I'm Ysolde Marrow, and I draw maps of the places the road forgets: woods that eat their own paths, barrows that open after dark, ravines the Kerchiefs think are theirs. [beat] Each one sworn under an oath. Each one ruled by something that won't want you there.

dlg.wayfinder.hub.0.note: A beat where the name would be. Approving.

dlg.wayfinder.hub.1.note: A beat where the name would be.

dlg.wayfinder.oaths.0.note: A cartographer's precision. 'Those are the choices.' dry gallows humour.

dlg.wayfinder.places.0.note: Rules laid out briskly. 'I sell them fewer maps.' deadpan.

dlg.wayfinder.drawn.0.note: Plain trade. The dead drawn 'from where their light went out' quieter, almost tender.

dlg.wayfinder.notes.0.note: Vague list, a little too light. Pause. Then lower, almost a warning: 'So has he.'

dlg.wayfinder.cb_opened_vault.0.note: Dry, with real fear under 'that far down'.

dlg.wayfinder.say_calling.2.note: 'I've a margin for people like you.' dry and ominous.

dlg.wayfinder.say_calling.3.note: Pointing at the map. A joke at the reavers.

dlg.wayfinder.say_calling.4.note: Pointing at the map. A joke at the reavers.

dlg.wayfinder.t_wayfinder.0.note: 'Once.' The facts, plain. 'My brother didn't.' steady. 'I still can't get the corners right.' dry, and it hurts.

dlg.wayfinder.margin.0.intent: asks your name for the margin
dlg.wayfinder.margin.0.note: Light because practised. 'put you down' means write, and also the other thing: she never hears the second meaning. Narrator: the pen.
dlg.wayfinder.margin.0.beats: Who came back, from where, how long they lasted, what they carried out. [beat] Name first; [beat] I'm a tidy woman. | Speaking of which. [beat] How do I put you down?

dlg.wayfinder.margin_name.0.note: Narrator for the writing and blotting. 'There.' A little ceremony in the last line.

dlg.wayfinder.margin_nobody.0.note: On audio the capital N vanishes: give the second 'Nobody' the same name-shape and weight she gave it as she wrote it, with a tiny beat before it; then 'More than most' lands the joke. Deadpan, no chill added.
dlg.wayfinder.margin_nobody.0.beats: Nobody. | You'd be surprised how often [beat] Nobody comes back. [beat] More than most.

dlg.wayfinder.margin_lark.0.hides: by making a name up she chooses not to sell you: a kindness she won't own
dlg.wayfinder.margin_lark.0.note: Edinburgh dry and quick, not fond teasing. The kindness is in the choice, not the voice.
dlg.wayfinder.margin_lark.0.beats: Lark. [beat] You look like a Lark. Larks get up early, [beat] and make a great deal of noise about it.
